intro: This is tslaws. You write the laws in TypeScript, an agent writes the code, and every change is checked against your laws before it lands.
basic: Here is a small project with five laws. tslaws is checking them now, with proofs, property tests and counterexamples.
fails: One law fails. The sort function drops duplicate numbers.
shrunk: The counterexample is shrunk to the smallest input that breaks the law, with a seed to reproduce it. An agent gets exactly what it needs to fix the code.
proved: This law is proved. A Z3 proof says it holds for every number, not just a sample.
tested: This one is tested: a couple of hundred generated inputs, and a recorded seed to replay any failure.
react: Now a React app. Component laws and end-to-end laws run in a real browser.
all: Component, accessibility, speed and model laws all report in one dashboard.
a11y: Accessibility: axe-core audits the real rendered board, for every generated state.
speed: Speed: adding a task has a time budget, measured in the browser, on boards of up to two hundred tasks.
block: And it must not block the main thread. Long tasks are measured in the page.
rerun: Run everything again, and watch the real page under test, live, while each law runs.
watch: Edit a file, and the laws rerun on their own.
outro: Install it with npm i dash D tslaws. TypeScript stays TypeScript, and the laws stay yours.
